text:
Predicates:
Visa(x, y) ::: x has a visa y.
Apply(x, y, z) ::: x needs to apply for z if x wants to work in y.
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
Work(x, y) ::: x wants to work in y.
Mike ::: Mike is an international student.
Premises:
∀x (Student(x) ∧ International(x, US) → (Visa(x, F1) ∨ Visa(x, J1))) ::: International students in US have either an F1 visa or a J1 visa.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ International(x, US) ∧ Visa(x, F1) ∧ Work(x, US) → Apply(x, US, CPT) ∨ Apply(x, US, OPT)) ::: An international student in US with an F1 visa needs to apply for CPT or OPT if the student wants to work in the US.
Mike ∧ Student(Mike) ::: Mike is an international student.
Apply(Mike, US, CPT) ::: Mike needs to apply for CPT if he wants to work in the US.
Conclusion:
Visa(Mike, F1) ::: Mike has an F1 visa.
